result.rationale: The diff in EventManager.create shows `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed immediately by `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")` — no optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null/[] (now possible, e.g. handleNewBooking sets it to null, confirm/editLocation handlers set []), destructuring yields undefined and reading `.integration` throws TypeError, breaking the previously guarded fallback (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== ...`). Mechanism fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: EventManager.create destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` unguarded, so a null or empty-array destinationCalendar throws instead of triggering the documented Cal Video fallback. A booking or confirmation with location integrations:google_meet and no destinationCalendar — the exact case the fallback comment describes, and now the null emitted by handleNewBooking and the [] emitted by confirm.handler/editLocation — throws TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')" and fails the request, where the old `?.` code silently fell back to Cal Video.
